messages.body_plain:
Hi Iñaki,

I have to admit I'm still quite a bit confused what is going on behind the scenes here, and I'm hoping to understand a little better. I've narrowed the problem I'm having even further. Here I have just one resource and I only include the 25 initial conditions at time 0. All of the entities should leave the system at time 5. However as seen from the graph, most of the entities do not get untrapped at t = 5. By tracking the delays, I can see that after t = 5, the delay attribute is calculated to be negative (because it's calculating when it should have left the system from the current time). Then when timeout_from_attribute() is called, the delay is coerced to positive, and so these entities never leave the system.

Uncommenting the add_dataframe() command  sends more signals so it is easier to see how these delays are being calculated. Looking at the attrbs dataframe i see the delay is actually because calculating correctly up until t = 5 for these initial entities (delay + current time = 5).

This behaviour is fixed by uncommenting either the first send() command in trj or uncommenting the delay <- max(0,delay) line in the handler.

My question is why does adding another send() command at t = 0 affect whether or not these entities get untrapped 5 time units later? And why do the entities stay stuck in the system without that send() command?

library(simmer)
library(simmer.plot)

tmax <- 100

handlr <- trajectory()%>%
  set_attribute(c("start", "delay"), function() {

    left <- sum(get_attribute(envs, c("start", "delay"))) - now(envs)

    delay <- left
    #delay <- max(0,delay)
    c(now(envs), delay)

  })%>%
  timeout_from_attribute("delay")

trj <- trajectory()%>%

  #send("sgnl") %>%

  seize("resrc")%>%
  set_attribute(c("start","delay") , function()
    c(now(envs), 5))%>%

  trap("sgnl", handlr)%>%
  send("sgnl")%>%
  untrap("sgnl") %>%
  release("resrc")

envs <- simmer()

data <- data.frame(time = replicate(1000, rexp(1, 10)))
init <- replicate(25, 0)

envs%>%

  add_resource("resrc", Inf, Inf)%>%

  add_generator("initial entities", trj, at(init), mon = 2) %>%

  #add_dataframe("signallers", trj, data)%>%

  run(until = tmax)

resrcs <- get_mon_resources(envs)
plot(resrcs, metric = "usage")

attrbs <- get_mon_attributes(envs)
plot(attrbs)

Thanks again,

Sam

messages.subject: Re: [simmer-devel] Issue with signalling
messages.body_plain:
As we discussed in previous examples, simultaneous arrivals are not
going to work in general with this pattern, because there are so many
things happening at the same time, and event order is not guaranteed
anymore. In other words, signaling with simultaneous events causes
undefined behaviour. But this is a general problem of DES, and the
only way to properly fix it is to avoid simultaneous arrivals
altogether.

And if you really really want to know what's going on, you can set
`envs <- simmer(verbose=TRUE)`.

messages.subject: Generate retries (new arrivals) without removing original arrival from queues
messages.subject_clean: Generate retries (new arrivals) without removing original arrival from queues
messages.body_plain:
Hi everyone,

I am currently trying to realize a simulation in which a source generates requests to a system. If these requests are not processed within a certain timeframe (30 seconds), the source generates a new request. Thereby, the initial request is not removed from the system, instead, both requests are processed. Ideally, I would be able to track which requests are issued by which source so that I can track how many retries were needed before successful completion.

Is there a intended mechanism in simmer that allows the generation of new arrivals based on the current sojourn time of a previous arrival?

I tried using `renege_in`, but even with `keep_seized = T` this seems to remove the arrival from the queue.

So ideally, I would like to create a new arrival every time any previous arrival has been in the system for exactly n seconds without removing the original arrival.

Any idea how I could achieve this?

messages.body_plain:
Closest I managed to get is the following. The problem here is, however, that renege_abort() within the out trajectory of a renege_if does not abort the renege, so I still lose the original event.

     library(simmer)

     env <- simmer() %>%
       add_global("nDevices", 0) %>%
       add_global("nRetries", 0)

     trj_initial <- trajectory() %>%
       set_attribute("device", function() get_global(env, "nDevices")) %>%
       set_global("nDevices", 1, "+") %>%
       renege_in(t = 30, out = trajectory() %>% log_("Retry") %>% activate("retry") %>% set_global("retry_device", function() get_attribute(env, "device")) %>% renege_abort()) %>%
       seize("cpu") %>%
       timeout(20) %>%
       release("cpu") %>%
       log_("Finished")

     trj_retry <- trajectory() %>%
       deactivate("retry") %>%
       set_attribute("device", function() get_global(env, "retry_device")) %>%
       renege_in(t = 30, out = trajectory() %>% log_("Retry") %>% renege_abort()) %>%
       seize("cpu") %>%
       timeout(20) %>%
       release("cpu") %>%
       log_("Finished")

     trj_setup <- trajectory() %>%
       deactivate("retry")

     env %>%
       add_resource("cpu", capacity = 1) %>%
       add_generator("initial", trj_initial, distribution = at(0, 1), mon = 2) %>%
       add_generator("setup", trj_setup, distribution = at(0)) %>%
       add_generator("retry", trj_retry, distribution = function() 0)

     env %>%
       reset() %>%
       run(until = 120)

messages.body_plain:
I think I solved it using clone() and signaling.

The code below achieves what I was trying to do. The idea is to clone each arrival that remove the clone via leave if the original has been processed within the timeout. Otherwise, the timeout runs out and the retry is triggered by activating the retry generator for a single arrival. I would still be interested to know if there is a simpler, more elegant solution to this. Maybe something like async_timeout or timeout(blocking = FALSE) could be used to make this simpler?

       library(simmer)

       retry_on <- F
       retry_vec <- c()

       env <- simmer() %>%
         add_global("nDevices", 0) %>%
         add_global("nRetries", 0)

       trj_initial <- trajectory() %>%
         set_attribute("device", function() get_global(env, "nDevices")) %>%

         set_global(function() paste0("nRetries_device_", get_attribute(env, "device")), 0) %>%

         set_global("nDevices", 1, "+") %>%

         log_(function() paste0("Arrival of intial of device ", get_attribute(env, "device"))) %>%
         clone(2,
               trajectory() %>%

                 seize("cpu") %>%
                 timeout(20) %>%
                 release("cpu") %>%

                 send(function() paste0(get_name(env))) %>%
                 log_("Initial Finished"),
               trajectory() %>%
                 trap(function() paste0(get_name(env)), handler = trajectory() %>% leave(1, keep_seized = F)) %>%
                 timeout(30) %>%
                 log_(function() paste0("Trigger retry of device ", get_attribute(env, "device"))) %>%
                 timeout(function() { retry_vec <<- c(retry_vec, get_attribute(env, "device")); return(0) }) %>%
                 timeout(function() { retry_on <<- T; return(0) }) %>%
                 activate("retry"))

       trj_retry <- trajectory() %>%
         deactivate("retry") %>%

         timeout(function() { retry_on <<- F; return(0) }) %>%
         set_attribute("device", function() { i <- retry_vec[1]; retry_vec <<- tail(retry_vec, -1); return(i) }) %>%
         set_global(function() paste0("nRetries_device_", get_attribute(env, "device")), 1, "+") %>%
         log_(function() paste0("Arrival of retry of device ", get_attribute(env, "device"))) %>%
       clone(2,
               trajectory() %>%

                 seize("cpu") %>%
                 timeout(20) %>%
                 release("cpu") %>%

                 send(function() paste0(get_name(env))) %>%
                 log_("Retry Finished"),
               trajectory() %>%
                 trap(function() paste0(get_name(env)), handler = trajectory() %>% leave(1, keep_seized = F)) %>%
                 timeout(30) %>%
                 log_(function() paste0("Trigger retry of device ", get_attribute(env, "device"))) %>%
                 timeout(function() { retry_vec <<- c(retry_vec, get_attribute(env, "device")); return(0) }) %>%
                 timeout(function() { retry_on <<- T; return(0) }) %>%
                 activate("retry"))

       env %>%
         add_resource("cpu", capacity = 1) %>%

         add_generator("initial", trj_initial, distribution = at(0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5)) %>%
         add_generator("retry", trj_retry, distribution = function() ifelse(retry_on, 0, -1))

       env %>%
         reset() %>%

         run(until = 1000)

messages.body_plain:
Brilliant solution! A very clever use of clone(). :) Additionally,
there's a helper called when_activated() that generates n arrivals
when an activate() activity is called upon the generator (see examples
under ?when_activated). It doesn't require deactivation, or keeping
track of retries, so it could simplify your code notably.

messages.body_plain:
Thank you for the hint regarding when_activated(). Really helpful!

I now have one last question regarding the monitoring of clones: Is there a way to only monitor the original? synchronize() provides the mon_all and wait flags, but I can't tell ahead of time if the original or the clone is going to be finished first. Ideally, I would like to only have the original included in the arrival results.

Right now, I just don't synchronize() at all and filter for finished == T afterwards since the clones all leave() the system. However, that doesn't seem to be always consistent and also conflicts with arrivals still in the system after the simulation time ends.

Any hints are much appreciated!

messages.body_plain:
On Mon, 24 Aug 2020 at 11:23, 's-geissler' via simmer-devel
<simmer...@googlegroups.com> wrote:
>
> I now have one last question regarding the monitoring of clones: Is there a way to only monitor the original? synchronize() provides the mon_all and wait flags, but I can't tell ahead of time if the original or the clone is going to be finished first. Ideally, I would like to only have the original included in the arrival results.

Unfortunately, this is not possible currently.

> Right now, I just don't synchronize() at all and filter for finished == T afterwards since the clones all leave() the system. However, that doesn't seem to be always consistent and also conflicts with arrivals still in the system after the simulation time ends.

One thing you could do is to make clones wait() forever. Then, they
are not scheduled anymore and they don't appear in the output
statistics. Or you could set an attribute before leaving, so that you
can identify those clones. Or, given that clones do not seize
anything, they won't appear in get_mon_arrivals(per_resource=TRUE),
which is the most interesting table, I believe, for your main
arrivals.

--
Iñaki Úcar
